source.notes: Human-source-first adaptation. Wrong-work-group-chat send, rapid deletion, 40+ viewers and coworker private check-in are retained as source facts. Korean wording and generic workplace staging are localized adaptations. The source author's later explanation is intentionally omitted; ending is silent embarrassment.

episode_only.identity_digest: Mid-20s Korean woman; shoulder-length straight dark-brown hair with soft inward ends and an off-center part; slightly rounded everyday face; cream short-sleeve T-shirt under a muted sage service apron, dark straight pants, slim-normal build, no glasses or jewelry; intentionally ordinary and non-glamorous.

slides.beat: A difficult customer situation becomes awkward enough that a coworker calmly steps in to help.
slides.action: worker_01 stands behind the counter visibly uncomfortable while an agitated customer gestures across the counter; a one-frame coworker calmly steps between the interaction without violence or theatrics.
scene_facts: worker_01 must use the locked episode-only identity digest and v2 drawing language
the customer is a one-frame ordinary adult extra, not threateningly villainous or physically violent
a one-frame helper coworker calmly intervenes and is visually distinct from worker_01 and all recurring leads
the location is a simple generic service counter with low-detail background
no readable menu, logo, signage, caption, dialogue, or speech bubble is baked into the raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer immediately understands that worker_01 just had an uncomfortable customer interaction and another coworker helped.
slides.composition: 4:5 medium-wide eye-level scene from a slight side angle; worker_01 remains the emotional focus, helper coworker creates a clear spatial buffer, customer stays secondary; reserve no major text zone because this beat should read visually.
slides.visual_delta_from_previous: OPENING: establishes the uncomfortable customer interaction and coworker intervention.

slides.beat: After the incident, worker_01 goes to a quiet staff nook and opens the messenger to tell friends about what happened.
slides.location: simple staff nook behind the workplace
slides.action: worker_01 sits alone on a small bench or stool, shoulders dropping after the tense interaction, phone in both hands as she begins typing.
scene_facts: worker_01 identity, apron, hair and clothing remain exactly continuous from slide 1
she is now alone and visibly decompressing rather than panicking
phone is present and clearly the next story object
staff nook is simple and lower-detail than the character
phone screen contains only blank/simple interface shapes; no readable text is baked into the raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer understands she is privately messaging someone after the incident.
slides.composition: 4:5 medium shot from slightly above and behind one shoulder, allowing the phone and relaxed shoulders to read while keeping a clean screen/text overlay zone.
slides.visual_delta_from_previous: SPATIAL+EMOTION: moves from public counter conflict to private decompression in the staff nook.

screen_contract.subject_screen_relation: worker_01 looks at the physical display face while holding the phone naturally.
screen_contract.camera_screen_relation: camera may see the phone edge/back or only a limited oblique glimpse; full UI readability is not required.
screen_contract.geometry_contract: The phone display remains on the physical front face. Do not expose the full screen by twisting the handset away from worker_01.

slides.beat: She sends the message, immediately notices it went to the workplace group, and the read-status begins collapsing almost at once.
slides.action: worker_01 holds the phone naturally toward herself; her face snaps from casual focus to horrified realization. A separate UI inset/overlay at one side shows the KakaoTalk-inspired group-chat shell, the just-sent message area, workplace-group context, and rapidly decrementing/disappearing read-status numerals.
scene_facts: worker_01 identity, apron, hair and clothing remain exactly continuous from slide 2
old separate send and realization beats are intentionally merged because their visual delta was too small
the physical phone remains naturally oriented toward worker_01; the audience does not need to read its physical display
screen information is carried by one separate UI inset/overlay inside the same panel, not by a second comic panel
the UI shell is KakaoTalk-inspired for contemporary Korean everyday messaging, without copied logo/wordmark
actual message text, room title, reaction text and decrementing/disappearing read-status numerals belong to vector/layout, not raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer instantly understands that she sent the message to the wrong workplace group and people are already reading it.
slides.composition: 4:5 medium-close reaction shot; worker_01's face/body owns the scene while a compact UI inset sits to one side. The physical handset stays naturally facing her.
slides.visual_delta_from_previous: ACTION+INFORMATION: sending becomes immediate wrong-chat realization; previous S03/S04 were merged after low visual-delta review.

screen_contract.subject_screen_relation: worker_01 looks at the real display face; the handset is oriented for her, not for the audience.
screen_contract.camera_screen_relation: camera prioritizes worker_01 reaction and may see only back/edge/oblique handset; UI information is shown separately as an inset.
screen_contract.geometry_contract: Never put chat UI on the phone back and never rotate the handset into an audience-facing presentation pose. Reaction and UI are separated spatially.

slides.beat: She deletes immediately, but the group-read state shows that the message already spread too far.
slides.action: over-shoulder or adjacent POV relationship from behind/near worker_01 lets both her and the camera see the physical phone display face while she performs one simple delete action.
scene_facts: worker_01 and phone remain continuous from slide 3
this is screen-information-led: choose a physically valid over-shoulder/POV screen-readable view
the physical display face is visible to worker_01 and camera from compatible directions
the UI shell is KakaoTalk-inspired; deleted-message state and read/unread count are later vector content
no readable system text, room title, message, logo, numeral or speech bubble is baked into the raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer understands that she deletes the message but it is already too late.
slides.composition: 4:5 over-shoulder/POV-biased screen-information shot. Phone display is naturally visible to both worker_01 and camera; her face need not be frontal.
slides.visual_delta_from_previous: VIEWPOINT+ACTION: changes from reaction-led merged realization to a physically screen-readable deletion shot.

screen_contract.subject_screen_relation: worker_01 directly sees the display face while deleting.
screen_contract.camera_screen_relation: camera is placed over/near her shoulder so it can also see the same display face without reversing the phone.
screen_contract.geometry_contract: Character and camera share a plausible view of the display face. No back-screen hybrid and no front-facing reaction requirement.

slides.beat: A coworker privately messages her asking if she is okay and what happened.
slides.action: worker_01 freezes with the phone held naturally toward herself; her face/body shows mortified stillness. A small separate UI inset carries the private-message information.
scene_facts: worker_01 identity and outfit remain continuous
the coworker exists only through later vector chat text; do not invent a physical second person
the handset stays naturally oriented to worker_01; do not turn the screen toward the audience
a separate KakaoTalk-inspired DM inset reserves space for two short later messages
expression is mortified and frozen, not frantic, angry or tearful
no readable DM text, sender name, logo or speech bubble is baked into the raster
slides.story_clarity: The viewer understands someone from work has already privately contacted her about the accidental message.
slides.composition: 4:5 medium reaction shot with face fully readable and handset natural; DM information sits in a compact separate UI inset.
slides.visual_delta_from_previous: EMOTION+INFORMATION: changes from active deletion to frozen mortification after a private coworker message.

screen_contract.subject_screen_relation: worker_01 looks at the physical display face held toward herself.
screen_contract.camera_screen_relation: camera prioritizes her face/body; physical screen may be oblique or hidden, with DM information supplied by inset.
screen_contract.geometry_contract: Do not make worker_01 show the private phone to the audience. Use the declared inset for message readability.

slides.beat: She says absolutely nothing and is overwhelmed by embarrassment.
slides.action: worker_01 folds inward on the bench, torso bent, face buried in both hands or nearly hidden, shoulders raised, visibly flushed; the phone rests beside her or stays secondary with no screen information.
scene_facts: worker_01 identity, hair, apron and clothing remain continuous even with face partly hidden
final emotion must read as extreme embarrassment through whole-body pose
strong expressive pose is allowed within style
phone is secondary and its screen is not story information
no reply, narration, internal monologue, reaction text, caption, message or speech bubble appears
slides.story_clarity: The viewer understands she is so embarrassed she wants to disappear, without explanatory words.
slides.composition: 4:5 slightly high wider reaction shot showing the whole folded posture; phone is secondary; allow empty breathing room.
slides.visual_delta_from_previous: EMOTIONAL_LANDING: moves from frozen phone reaction to fully embodied silent embarrassment.

set_qc: Judge the completed sequence for viewer-perceived directional/compositional redundancy rather than fixed direction quotas.
Adjacent beats must have a defensible visual delta; UI-state-only continuations are merge candidates.
For every screen-bearing slide, verify information owner, display-face geometry, subject gaze, camera visibility and UI delivery mode.
No device may show UI on its back/case, and no private handset may be twisted toward the audience without story justification.
Korean everyday messaging defaults to a KakaoTalk-inspired UI profile unless explicit story context overrides it.
visual_direction.reflection_policy: No story-relevant mirror/reflection is required in this episode; incidental reflections must remain plausible.
visual_direction.skin_color_policy: Main/supporting characters share the same flat local-color grammar; no automatic yellow/orange/sepia cast.
visual_direction.notes: Revised after prototype QC: old send/realization slides were merged; screen information and character reaction are separated by declared information ownership and physically valid screen contracts.
